Currently using simp only [← zify_simps] does the same as simp only [zify_simps]:

import Mathlib

example (x y : ℕ) : x - y = 0 := by
  simp only [← zify_simps]
  simp only [Int.ofNat_inj]
  sorry

Is it possible somehow to modify the attribute, so that simp only [← zify_simps] does the reverse?
zify here is just for argument sake - I am interested in cases where there is no clear simp normal form, but two obvious candidates (1 vs Equiv.refl, * vs Equiv.trans, etc)

Currently simp sets only index the forward direction, so to support this there would need to be two simp sets.

Running a whole simp set in reverse is probably not a good idea for most simp sets, since they'll usually have lemmas that diverge in reverse.

Something I could see is having a feature to register which simp set is the "reverse" of a given simp set, that way if you do ← zify_simps you'd actually get unzify_simps, or what have you, though given that unzify_simps isn't especially onerous to write, it'd be a very low priority feature unless it enables something non-obvious and interesting.

One thing that could be interesting is if registering a lemma with @[zify_simps] would auto-register @[unzify_simps <-], but I'd worry about bad unzify_simps lemmas being silently added this way. There would need to be some attribute syntax to disable this at least. In any case, it's not especially difficult to write @[zify_simps, unzify_simps <-] for truly bidirectional lemmas.
